title: A public notice for earthquake safety
intro: Yanig means "tremor" in Tagalog. Yanig is a free website about earthquake safety in the Philippines.

does.title: What Yanig does
items: It shows recent earthquakes near the Philippines on a map and in a list.
It gives safety steps for before, during and after an earthquake.
It lists emergency hotlines for cities in the Philippines.
It shows earthquake news from news sites.
It has a checklist for your emergency kit.

doesNot.title: What Yanig does not do
items: Yanig does not send alerts, notifications or warnings.
Yanig cannot predict earthquakes. No one can.
Yanig is not an official source of earthquake information.

data.title: Where the data comes from
data.intro: Your browser gets earthquake data directly from three agencies. Yanig checks for new data every 10 minutes.
data.estimate: The first magnitude and place of an earthquake are estimates. The agencies can change them later.

geonet.name: GeoNet
geonet.text: Earthquakes in and near New Zealand.

bmkg.name: BMKG
bmkg.text: Recent large earthquakes in and near Indonesia.

official.title: For official reports, go to PHIVOLCS
official.text1: PHIVOLCS is the official Philippine agency for earthquakes and volcanoes.
official.text2: Yanig does not use PHIVOLCS data. For official earthquake reports in the Philippines, use PHIVOLCS.

offline.title: Without internet
items: Pages you opened before work without internet.
The earthquake list and news can be old until you are online again.
You can add Yanig to the home screen of your phone. Then it opens like an app.

languages.title: Languages
languages.text: Yanig is in English, Tagalog, Spanish and Japanese. The privacy notice and the terms are in English and Tagalog only.

maker.title: Who made Yanig
items: Yanig is free. You do not need an account.
The source code is on GitHub under the MIT License.

news.title: Earthquake news
news.intro: News about earthquakes from news sites around the world, in English. Yanig gets the list from NewsAPI.
news.sourceNote: Other news sites write these articles. Yanig does not write or check them.
